title: better-auth/electron sign-in response exposes server secrets and can bypass two-factor
summary: A normal desktop sign-in can return the server auth context rather than the normal response, disclosing the auth secret and configured social-provider client secrets to a user who can sign in. With the auth secret, the user can create trusted signed values and obtain another known-email user’s session. Separately, when the Electron plugin precedes twoFactor(), password sign-in is enabled, and the account has two-factor enabled, a desktop sign-in code can be exchanged for a full session before second-factor completion. The advisory documents these separate paths under one GHSA; no CVE is assigned.
ai_role: Discovered by Anthropic’s OSS Scanner, ANT-2026-R8Z0P3MG. The advisory also lists ANT-2026-DDHILQ2X as a related anonymous-sign-in path, but does not establish it as an independent vulnerability.
classification_note: The vulnerability is documented as a public disclosure; the source does not establish prior defender knowledge or exploitation.
remediation_note: Upgrade @better-auth/electron and better-auth to 1.7.16 or 1.8.0-beta.5. If previously deployed, rotate auth and social-provider secrets.

impacts.conditions: Affected Electron plugin; a user who can sign in can cause the wrong endpoint context to be returned.
Password sign-in enabled; user has two-factor; electron() is registered before twoFactor(); attacker knows the user password.
